audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave one side all seven stages while the two layers disagreed about which side: full phases[N].side read Fizz on every row, content win[N] read Xerath on every row, and the packet flags the 7/0 sweep against a 47.65% win rate.
audit.why: Levels 1-5 are genuinely Xerath's: Q reaches 750 and Fizz's longest laning tool is Urchin Strike at 550, so he cannot answer poke. From level 6 that reverses — Chum the Waters throws 1300 units, grounds and knocks up, and Playful / Trickster goes untargetable through Shocking Orb, which is why the matchup sits under 50%.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 to Xerath (win[N] already Xerath, so side only). Rows 4-6 to Fizz, with win[4..6], phases[4..6].why and whys[4..6] rewritten in the same proposal to describe Fizz winning.
sources: kits: Xerath Q 750, Fizz Q 550 / R 1300

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and first-item rows were written as Xerath spikes and ignored the bigger spike on the other side of the lane.
audit.why: Chum the Waters is 120/100/80s and converts every one of his gap-closers into a guaranteed combo; Rite of the Arcane immobilises you for its duration and any CC ends the channel.
audit.corrected: phases[4..6].why now name Chum the Waters, its 80s late cooldown, and the fact that your R is channelled while he arrives.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions were named but never stated: Playful / Trickster makes him untargetable so your Shocking Orb and R barrages pass through him, Chum the Waters grounds and knocks up and so cancels your R channel, and Seastone Trident is an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions flags autoreset-burst-tell for this matchup; the kit flags E untargetable and R knockup/grounding against an owner R flagged channel/interruptible.
audit.corrected: cooldowns and dosFull[0].d now carry the real numbers and the untargetable/channel interaction; Seastone Trident's reset is stated in dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dontsFull[1].d called your E a 'fourteen second' cooldown when Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 falling to 11s.
audit.why: The window you play around is Playful / Trickster's 16s at rank 1 down to 8s at rank 5 — that is the number that decides when you may step up.
audit.corrected: Both fields now carry sourced cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Each title promises one thing and the body answered another.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten from Fizz's kit to answer their own titles.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane online — chipped targets anywhere in the lane's zip code are now finishable. Shove and snipe.
edits.after: Chum the Waters plus Playful / Trickster is a kill on you at 6, and your R channel is where he lands.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-W chunks third-bars. He farms at half HP forever or he doesn't farm.
edits.after: One landed Chum the Waters at first item ends you long before your Q-W chip matters.

edits.before: Late Xerath wins fights from the next postal code: stun the entry, barrage the objective, and never be seen.
edits.after: He flanks on an 80-second Chum the Waters; once he reaches you, distance stops mattering and the fight is his.

edits.before: Level 6 your off-screen ult poke keeps chunking him when you play max range.
edits.after: Level 6 his Chum the Waters into E combo kills you through your ult channel.

edits.before: On first item your farm and poke lead holds if you save E for after his E.
edits.after: On first item one landed Chum the Waters ends you before your poke lead pays.

edits.before: Late your ranged poke and DPS beat him whenever he fails to reach you.
edits.after: Late his flank finds you eventually, and one clean reach is all he needs.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Check it before every step-up. - E Shocking Orb is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Playful / Trickster: 16s at rank 1, 8s at rank 5 — untargetable, so Shocking Orb and R barrages pass through him. Step up after it is spent. - Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1, your only 'no'. - Chum the Waters, 120/100/80s, grounds and knocks up: it ends your R channel.

edits.before: Fizz wins by landing Playful / Trickster, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Fizz wins by hopping Playful / Trickster over your stun, then landing Chum the Waters — grounded, you cannot channel or walk.

edits.before: The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: A centred wave keeps you outside 550-range Urchin Strike, so he has to spend Playful / Trickster just to close the gap he starts in.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and whiffs through his untargetable hop — hold it for the landing frame after Playful / Trickster.

edits.before: Your E is a single 'no' per fourteen seconds — spent on poke, every assassin and fighter in the lobby hears the silence.
edits.after: Shocking Orb is one 'no' per 13 seconds at rank 1 — spent on poke, his 8-second Playful / Trickster arrives to silence.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: His combo opens on a Seastone Trident auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell — at half HP that animation is already the start of your death.

edits.before: If Fizz opens the score, reset expectations and respect Playful / Trickster doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with max-range Qs and stay relevant through R snipes.
edits.after: A fed Fizz kills through Zhonya's on an 80-second Chum the Waters, so never hold a wave past the centre line. Farm at 750 range, keep a ward on your flank, and stay relevant through R snipes.

notes: The packet already flagged the contradiction: 47.65% win rate against a 7/0 chart. Adjudicated as a genuine split — Xerath owns levels 1-5 on range (750 Q vs 550 Urchin Strike), Fizz owns 6 onward on Chum the Waters. Rows 0-3 needed a side edit only, because content win[N] was already Xerath; rows 4-6 needed a win[N] edit only, because full side was already Fizz. Ratings left as they stand: I cannot tell from the kit whether the number describes the owner or the stage winner, and the chart rule says leave rather than guess. spikes[] and the content early/mid/late prose already describe the post-6 flip correctly, so they needed no change.
